chunks.text: شکایات کا ازالہ: برانچ اسٹاف کے لیے رہنما
headingPath: شکایات کا ازالہ: برانچ اسٹاف کے لیے رہنما

chunks.text: یہ رہنما برانچ کے عملے کے لیے ہے۔ اس میں بتایا گیا ہے کہ کسٹمر کی شکایت کیسے سنی جائے، کیسے درج کی جائے، اور کب اسے آگے بھیجا جائے۔ ہر شکایت ایک موقع ہے: جو کسٹمر شکایت کرتا ہے وہ ابھی بینک چھوڑنا نہیں چاہتا۔

جب کوئی کسٹمر ناراض ہو تو پہلے اسے پوری بات کہنے دیں۔ درمیان میں نہ ٹوکیں۔ آواز نیچی رکھیں اور آہستہ بولیں۔ جب کسٹمر بات ختم کر لے تو ایک جملے میں دہرائیں: "آپ کہہ رہے ہیں کہ آپ کے اکاؤنٹ سے دو بار رقم کٹی ہے اور ایک بار واپس نہیں آئی۔ ٹھیک؟"

معذرت کرنا کمزوری نہیں ہے۔ "مجھے افسوس ہے کہ آپ کو یہ پریشانی ہوئی" کہنے سے آدھی ناراضی ختم ہو جاتی ہے۔ لیکن کبھی ایسا وعدہ نہ کریں جو آپ پورا نہیں کر سکتے۔

ہر شکایت سسٹم میں درج ہوتی ہے، کاغذ پر نہیں۔ درج کرتے وقت یہ معلومات لکھیں: کسٹمر کا نام، اکاؤنٹ کی قسم، تاریخ، رقم، اور کسٹمر کے اپنے الفاظ میں مسئلہ۔ کسٹمر کو شکایت نمبر لکھ کر دیں یا ایس ایم ایس کے ذریعے بھیجیں۔

شناختی کارڈ کا نمبر یا اکاؤنٹ نمبر کاؤنٹر پر بلند آواز میں نہ پڑھیں۔ تصدیق کے لیے صرف آخری چار ہندسے دہرائیں۔

کسٹمر کو بتائیں کہ جواب کب ملے گا۔ عام شکایات کے لیے معیار یہ ہے:

| شکایت کی قسم | پہلا جواب | حتمی حل |
| ------------------------------------- | --------- | --------------- |
| اے ٹی ایم سے رقم نہ نکلنا مگر کٹ جانا | اسی دن | سات کام کے دن |
| کارڈ پر غلط چارج | اسی دن | پندرہ کام کے دن |
| عملے کا رویہ | اسی دن | تین کام کے دن |
| اسٹیٹمنٹ میں غلطی | اسی دن | پانچ کام کے دن |

اگر وقت بڑھ جائے تو کسٹمر کو خود فون کریں۔ کسٹمر کا فون آنے سے پہلے آپ کا فون جانا چاہیے۔

یہ شکایات فوراً برانچ منیجر کو بھیجیں:

1. کسی بھی قسم کا فراڈ یا مشکوک لین دین۔
2. پچاس ہزار روپے سے زیادہ کی رقم کا تنازع۔
3. کسٹمر کا کہنا کہ عملے نے بدتمیزی کی۔
4. وہی کسٹمر جو ایک ماہ میں دوسری بار شکایت لے کر آیا ہو۔

آگے بھیجتے وقت کسٹمر کو منیجر سے خود ملوائیں۔ کسٹمر کو دوبارہ پوری کہانی نہ سنانی پڑے؛ ایک جملے میں خلاصہ منیجر کو خود بتائیں۔

جب کوئی بزرگ کسٹمر پریشانی میں برانچ آئے تو پہلے انہیں بیٹھنے کی جگہ دیں، پانی پیش کریں، تسلی سے بات سنیں، اور پھر قدم بہ قدم ان کا مسئلہ حل کریں۔ ان سے پوچھیں کہ وہ اردو میں بات کرنا چاہتے ہیں یا انگریزی میں۔ فارم خود بھریں اور ہر خانہ پڑھ کر سنائیں۔

- "یہ میرا کام نہیں" کہہ کر کسٹمر کو دوسرے کاؤنٹر بھیج دینا۔
- شکایت درج کیے بغیر زبانی وعدہ کرنا۔
- کسٹمر سے بحث کرنا کہ غلطی اس کی اپنی ہے۔
- وقت بتائے بغیر "جلد ہو جائے گا" کہنا۔

ایک کسٹمر کہتا ہے کہ اے ٹی ایم نے رقم نہیں دی لیکن اکاؤنٹ سے پانچ ہزار روپے کٹ گئے۔ آپ کیا کریں گے؟ پہلے معذرت کریں، پھر تاریخ، وقت اور اے ٹی ایم کی جگہ پوچھیں، شکایت درج کریں، شکایت نمبر دیں، اور بتائیں کہ رقم عموماً سات کام کے دنوں میں واپس آ جاتی ہے۔

ایک کسٹمر ایک ماہ میں دوسری بار اسی مسئلے کے ساتھ آیا ہے۔ آپ کیا کریں گے؟ اسے خود برانچ منیجر سے ملوائیں اور پچھلی شکایت کا نمبر ساتھ لے جائیں۔

journey.title: Handling Customer Complaints at the Branch

story.premise: Ayesha, a newly joined branch officer, must learn the art of handling customer complaints under the guidance of her senior colleague Farhan, facing a series of real situations that test her patience, judgment, and knowledge of procedure.
story.setting: A busy urban bank branch in Pakistan with a small counter hall, a manager's office, and a customer waiting area.

characters.name: Bilal
characters.role: Young customer with a repeat ATM complaint

outline.title: Handling Customer Complaints at the Branch
outline.summary: A training journey for branch staff on how to listen to, log, resolve, and escalate customer complaints professionally, with special attention to elderly customers and repeat complainants.

chapters.title: Listening First, Logging Right
chapters.arcBeat: New branch officer Ayesha learns the foundations of hearing out an upset customer and recording the complaint properly before anything else can happen.

missions.title: Calm the Storm
missions.objective: Practice active listening and empathetic response with an angry customer.

missions.title: Log It Right
missions.objective: Correctly log a complaint with all required details while protecting customer identity.

chapters.title: Timelines and Turning Points
chapters.arcBeat: Ayesha's mentor Farhan shows her how to set expectations with customers and recognize the moments a complaint must move up the chain.

missions.title: Promise the Right Time
missions.objective: Match complaint types to correct response and resolution timelines, and know when to call the customer proactively.

missions.title: Know When to Escalate
missions.objective: Decide which complaints require immediate escalation to the branch manager and perform a smooth handoff.

chapters.title: Care Beyond the Counter
chapters.arcBeat: An elderly customer named Ghulam Sarwar visits the branch distressed, testing whether Ayesha can apply extra care and avoid common pitfalls.

missions.title: Serve with Patience
missions.objective: Provide appropriate care to an elderly or distressed customer, including seating, language preference, and form assistance.

missions.title: Avoid the Trap
missions.objective: Identify and avoid common mistakes such as deflecting responsibility or making unlogged promises.

chapters.title: Putting It All Together
chapters.arcBeat: Ayesha faces two real branch cases that combine everything she has learned, proving she is ready to handle the counter on her own.

missions.title: The ATM Case
missions.objective: Resolve a full ATM cash dispute scenario from apology to complaint number to refund timeline.

missions.title: The Second Time Around
missions.objective: Handle a repeat complaint case by escalating correctly with prior complaint history, integrating all key concepts.

concepts.name: Active Listening and Empathy
concepts.summary: Let the customer finish speaking without interrupting, keep your voice low and calm, repeat back the issue in one sentence to confirm understanding, and apologize sincerely without making promises you cannot keep.

concepts.name: Logging a Complaint Correctly
concepts.summary: Every complaint must be logged in the system, not on paper, capturing customer name, account type, date, amount, and the issue in the customer's own words. Give the customer a complaint number by print or SMS, and protect identity by repeating only the last four digits of ID or account numbers aloud.

concepts.name: Response and Resolution Timelines
concepts.summary: Different complaint types have set standards for first response and final resolution, such as same-day first response for ATM cash-not-dispensed issues with seven working days for final resolution. If timelines slip, staff must proactively call the customer before the customer calls them.

concepts.name: When to Escalate to the Branch Manager
concepts.nameUr: برانچ منیجر کو رپورٹ کرنے کے حالات
concepts.summary: Certain complaints must be escalated immediately to the branch manager: any fraud or suspicious transaction, disputes over fifty thousand rupees, allegations of staff misbehavior, and repeat complaints from the same customer within a month.

concepts.name: Smooth Handoff During Escalation
concepts.nameUr: منیجر کے حوالے کرنے کا طریقہ
concepts.summary: When escalating, personally introduce the customer to the manager and summarize the issue in one sentence yourself so the customer does not have to repeat the whole story again.

concepts.name: Serving Elderly and Distressed Customers
concepts.nameUr: بزرگ اور پریشان کسٹمرز کی خدمت
concepts.summary: When an elderly or distressed customer arrives, offer them a seat and water, listen patiently, ask their preferred language, fill forms for them, and read out every field aloud before proceeding.

concepts.name: Common Mistakes to Avoid
concepts.nameUr: عام غلطیاں جن سے بچنا ہے
concepts.summary: Avoid telling customers 'this is not my job' and sending them elsewhere, making verbal promises without logging the complaint, arguing that the mistake is the customer's fault, or saying 'it will be done soon' without giving a specific timeframe.

concepts.name: Handling an ATM Cash Dispute
concepts.nameUr: اے ٹی ایم رقم کے تنازع کا حل
concepts.summary: For a customer reporting cash not dispensed but amount deducted, apologize first, ask for date, time and ATM location, log the complaint, provide a complaint number, and explain the typical seven working day refund period.

concepts.name: Handling a Repeat Complaint
concepts.nameUr: دوسری بار کی شکایت سے نمٹنا
concepts.summary: If a customer returns within a month with the same issue, escalate directly to the branch manager and bring along the number of the previous complaint.

roleplay.goal: Get an explanation and resolution for a double deduction from their account.
openers: Why was my money deducted twice from my account?
I've been coming here for years, and now you people take my money without explanation!
This is theft! Give me my money back right now or I'm closing my account and telling everyone!

behaviors.text: Stays quiet and lets the customer finish the full complaint before responding.
Speaks in a low, slow voice throughout the interaction.
Repeats the complaint back in one clear sentence to confirm understanding.
Apologizes for the trouble caused without promising a specific fix time.

callbacks.prompt: Before summarizing or apologizing, what must you always do first with an angry customer?
keyPoints: Let them finish speaking without interrupting.
Keep your voice low and speak slowly.

callbacks.prompt: When apologizing to a customer, what must you be careful not to do?
keyPoints: Do not promise something you cannot deliver.
Apologizing itself is fine and reduces anger, but keep promises realistic.

pack.objective: Practice active listening and empathetic response with an angry customer.

hints: Think about what happens when someone feels cut off mid-sentence.
The excerpt says not to interrupt and to keep your tone calm.
Letting them finish and staying quiet-voiced is the correct first step.
questions.prompt: The customer is speaking loudly and fast. What do you do first?

label.en: Let them finish speaking without interrupting
label.ur: انہیں بغیر ٹوکے پوری بات کہنے دیں
label.urLatn: Unhein baghair tokay poori baat kehne dein

options.consequence: The customer feels heard and slows down.

label.en: Interrupt to explain the bank's side immediately
label.ur: فوراً بینک کا موقف بتانے کے لیے بات کاٹ دیں
label.urLatn: Foran bank ka mauqaf batane ke liye baat kaat dein

options.consequence: The customer gets angrier, feeling ignored.

label.en: Raise your voice to match theirs so they take you seriously
label.ur: انہیں سنجیدہ لینے کے لیے اپنی آواز بھی اونچی کر دیں
label.urLatn: Unhein sanjeeda lene ke liye apni awaz bhi oonchi kar dein

variants.advanced: The customer is escalating quickly, cutting off your greeting. What is your first move?
variants.standard: The customer is speaking loudly and fast. What do you do first?
variants.foundation: The customer is upset and talking loudly. What is your first move?

questions.workedExample: A customer complains loudly about a double deduction. You stay silent, nod, and let them finish before speaking softly.

hints: Confirming understanding builds trust before you act.
A short one-sentence summary shows you were listening.
Try restating their issue back to them in your own words.
questions.prompt: After the customer finishes explaining, what should you do next?

label.en: Repeat the complaint back in one sentence to confirm
label.ur: شکایت کو ایک جملے میں دہرا کر تصدیق کریں
label.urLatn: Shikayat ko ek jumlay mein dohra kar tasdeeq karein

options.consequence: The customer confirms you understood and calms slightly.

label.ur: فوراً بینک کے طریقہ کار کی وضاحت شروع کریں
label.urLatn: Foran bank ke tareeqa-e-kaar ki wazahat shuru karein

options.consequence: The customer feels unheard and interrupts again.

label.en: Ask them to repeat everything again for clarity
label.ur: وضاحت کے لیے انہیں دوبارہ سب کچھ کہنے کو کہیں
label.urLatn: Wazahat ke liye unhein dobara sab kuch kehne ko kahein

options.consequence: The customer feels frustrated at having to repeat themselves.

variants.advanced: The customer has finished a long, detailed complaint. What is the best next step before offering a solution?
variants.standard: After the customer finishes explaining, what should you do next?
variants.foundation: The customer has stopped talking. What do you say next?

questions.workedExample: Customer says money was deducted twice. You say: 'You're saying two deductions happened and one wasn't refunded, correct?'

hints: An apology for the inconvenience is different from admitting fault.
Saying sorry can reduce anger, but don't commit to outcomes you can't control.
Choose the option that shows empathy without a firm promise.
questions.prompt: The customer is still upset after your summary. What should you say?

label.en: Say sorry for the trouble without promising a specific outcome
label.ur: مخصوص نتیجے کا وعدہ کیے بغیر پریشانی پر معذرت کریں
label.urLatn: Makhsoos nateeje ka wada kiye baghair pareshani par muzarat karein

options.consequence: The customer's anger eases without a broken promise later.

label.en: Promise the money will be refunded today
label.ur: وعدہ کریں کہ رقم آج ہی واپس ہو جائے گی
label.urLatn: Wada karein ke raqam aaj hi wapis ho jayegi

options.consequence: If it doesn't happen today, the customer feels betrayed.

label.en: Avoid apologizing since the bank may not be at fault
label.ur: معذرت سے گریز کریں کیونکہ ہو سکتا ہے قصور بینک کا نہ ہو
label.urLatn: Muzarat se gurez karein kyunke ho sakta hai qasoor bank ka na ho

options.consequence: The customer feels dismissed and gets angrier.

variants.advanced: The customer demands you guarantee the money is refunded today. How do you respond?
variants.standard: The customer is still upset after your summary. What should you say?
variants.foundation: What should you say to show empathy now?

questions.workedExample: You say: 'I'm sorry this happened to you' without promising when the refund will land.

teachBack.followUp: What should you do before you even reach the apology step?

keyPoints.text: Apologizing is not a weakness and reduces half the customer's anger.
You must still avoid promising outcomes you cannot guarantee.

Unique reference number assigned to each registered complaint for tracking and follow-up.
Initial acknowledgment provided to customer on the same day complaint is registered.
Complete solution to complaint provided within specified timeframe.
Business days excluding weekends and holidays for complaint resolution timeline.
Money in question between customer and bank regarding transaction or charge.
Process of forwarding complaint to higher authority when branch cannot resolve it.
National identification number that should not be announced loudly at counter.
Unique identifier for customer's bank account requiring confidential handling.
Final four numbers of account or card used for verification instead of full number.
Text message sent to customer's phone containing complaint number and details.
Transaction that appears fraudulent or unusual and requires immediate manager escalation.
Complaint regarding inappropriate behavior or rudeness by bank employee.
Service desk at branch where customers interact with staff for transactions.
Expression of regret to customer that helps resolve half of their dissatisfaction.
Technique of letting customer speak fully without interruption before responding.
Repeating customer's complaint in one sentence to confirm understanding.
Recording complaint in bank's digital system rather than on paper.
Proactive call made by staff to customer before they call to check complaint status.
Elderly customer requiring special care, seating, water, and step-by-step assistance.
